Why go: the most affordable private sail on Samui

King 9 is a small, simple sailing catamaran, and that is the point: it puts a private sail within reach of couples and small families. A 2.5-hour morning or sunset sail is long enough to swim, paddle and relax on a shaded deck without committing a whole day.

The night squid-fishing trip is the one most visitors haven't tried: the same method Samui's fishing boats use, with lights drawing squid to the surface after dark, and dinner on board.

Which sail to choose

The 2.5-hour morning sail is the calmest and coolest; the sunset sail runs from 16:00 to 18:30 and is the most popular with couples. The 4.5-hour half day goes to Koh Tan to snorkel, stops to fish and lands at Koh Madsum to see the pigs before sailing back. The full day from 10:00 to 18:30 gives time for all of this at a slower pace. Night squid fishing is a different experience altogether and works well as a last-night activity. Because the boat is small, it is quickly affected by wind; if the forecast looks rough, choose the morning sail, when the sea is usually calmest.

Who it suits

  • Couples and small families on a budget.
  • Anyone curious about local night fishing.
  • Guests who want a short sail before or after a beach day.

Who should choose something else

  • Groups wanting space, cabins and bathrooms: see the Vivienne or Gavina.
  • Anyone seasick in small boats on choppy days.

Good to know

  • Simple boat: expect a shaded deck rather than cabins.
  • Night fishing: bring insect repellent and a layer; it is cooler on the water at night.
  • Booking: online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thai time.
